dialogue.origin: 本日はお越しいただきありがとうございます。はじめにあなたの年齢と性別をお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.content: Thank you for coming in today. To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.origin: 22歳　男です
dialogue.content: I'm a 22-year-old man.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。本日はどのようなご相談でしょうか。
dialogue.content: Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.origin: お話しできるところからで大丈夫ですよ。
dialogue.content: You can start wherever you feel comfortable.

dialogue.origin: 職場や家庭で理不尽なことで責められてる人に助け舟を出してあげる勇気が出なくて黙り込んでしまい、そんな自分にストレスを感じます。
dialogue.content: At work and at home, when I see someone being unfairly blamed, I don't have the courage to step in and help. I just stay silent, and I feel stressed about myself for doing that.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。助けてあげたいのに思うようにできない自分にいら立ってしまうのですね。助けたい思いがある分苦しいですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So you feel frustrated with yourself for not being able to act the way you want to, even though you want to help. That desire to help is what makes it so painful.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです
dialogue.content: That's right.

dialogue.origin: どのような状況下少し具体的にお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.content: Could you tell me a little more specifically about the situations?

dialogue.origin: 状況か、ですね。失礼しました。
dialogue.content: The situations, that is. My apologies.

dialogue.origin: 家庭では、父母妹と現在同居しているのですが、母が精神科に通っていまして。父と妹それと近くに住んでいる父方の祖母はそれに理解がなく、甘えているだけお金の無駄だと言うんです。
dialogue.content: At home, I currently live with my parents and younger sister, and my mother is seeing a psychiatrist. My father, my sister, and my paternal grandmother who lives nearby don't understand. They say she's just being spoiled and it's a waste of money.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: 私はそれは違うし周りも理解して協力しなければ良くならないと思いつつ、父が怖くて何も言うことができません
dialogue.content: I believe that's wrong and that she won't get better unless those around her are understanding and cooperative, but I'm too scared of my father to say anything.

dialogue.origin: そうだったのですね。あなたはもっと理解を示すべきだと声をあげたいのにお父様が怖いと感じて行動に起こせずにいるのですね。
dialogue.content: I understand. So you want to speak up and say they should be more understanding, but you feel afraid of your father and can't bring yourself to act.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 行動に起こせない自分を責めてしまうのですね。それは苦しいですね。
dialogue.content: And you blame yourself for not being able to act. That must be very difficult.

dialogue.origin: 傷ついてる人が目の前にいて助けてあげれるはずなのに何もできなくて苦しいです
dialogue.content: It's painful to have someone hurting right in front of me, knowing I should be able to help, yet being unable to do anything.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね。相手を想う思いが人一倍ある分、外にそれを発揮できないのは苦しくなる一方だと思います。
dialogue.content: I can imagine. Since you care for others so deeply, it must only make it more painful when you can't express that outwardly.

dialogue.origin: 罪悪感などもわいてきます
dialogue.content: I also start to feel guilty.

dialogue.origin: 気が付く分、一人で抱えてしまいますよね。
dialogue.content: Because you're aware of it, you end up shouldering it all by yourself, don't you?

dialogue.origin: そうなんです。私のパートナーなど、理解がある人はいるのですが今遠距離なのですぐ相談できるような状況でもなく。
dialogue.content: That's right. I do have people who are understanding, like my partner, but we're in a long-distance relationship right now, so it's not a situation where I can easily talk to them.

dialogue.origin: 1人で抱え込みがちです
dialogue.content: I tend to bottle things up on my own.

dialogue.origin: そうだったのですね。ここでは少しでも多くの本音をお話くださいね。
dialogue.content: I see. Please feel free to share as many of your true feelings as you can here.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: Thank you.

dialogue.origin: 職場はどのような状況でしょうか？
dialogue.content: What is the situation like at work?

dialogue.origin: ある新人のバイトの女の子が、上司に教えてもらってすらないことで「これは普通こうだろ！」とか「これくらいやっとけ！」などと怒られたり、「新人なんだから全部我慢しなきゃだめだろ」と言われたりしていて
dialogue.content: There's a new part-time girl who gets yelled at by our boss for things she hasn't even been taught, with him saying things like, 'This is common sense!' or 'You should at least get this done!' and 'You're new, so you have to put up with everything.'

dialogue.origin: ええ。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 私は新人が出来ないのは当たり前だし、ましてや教えていないことができないのは上司の責任だと思うのですが、意見を言うことができず責められているのを傍観するしかできません。
dialogue.content: I think it's natural for a new person to not be able to do things, and I especially think it's the boss's fault when she can't do something she was never taught. But I can't voice my opinion and can only stand by and watch her get blamed.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。おっしゃるように、理不尽ととれる対応ですね。腹がたつ思いにもなると思います。
dialogue.content: I see. As you say, that does sound like an unreasonable way to treat someone. I can imagine it makes you angry as well.

dialogue.origin: そうですね、怒りもあると思います
dialogue.content: Yes, I think there's anger too.

dialogue.origin: それでもご家庭のことと同じく、上に物申せずにいるご自分を責めてしまうのでしょうか。
dialogue.content: And yet, just like with your family situation, do you blame yourself for not speaking up to a superior?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。
dialogue.content: Yes, I do.

dialogue.origin: 申し訳なく思います
dialogue.content: I feel bad about it.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか。助けてあげたいと思っているのに思うようにしてあげられないもどかしさと、自分を責めてしまう気持ちとを自宅でも職場でも毎日味わっていたら心がすり減る思いになりますよね。
dialogue.content: I see. Experiencing that frustration of wanting to help but not being able to, along with blaming yourself, every day at both home and work... it must be emotionally draining.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです。
dialogue.content: It is.

dialogue.origin: あまり気が抜ける場がないように感じます
dialogue.content: I feel like there's hardly any place where I can relax.

dialogue.origin: 自分のことではなく、他者のことに色々と思いをはせて怒りや罪悪感などを感じるのは、とても疲れますし無力感も感じることですよね。
dialogue.content: Feeling so much for others—anger, guilt, and so on—when it's not even about you, is very tiring and can make you feel powerless, can't it?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。すごく精神的に疲れてるような気がします。
dialogue.content: Yes. I feel like I'm very mentally exhausted.

dialogue.origin: 当然のことですよ。
dialogue.content: That's completely understandable.

dialogue.origin: でも、全て放り投げて見ないことにせず、まだ何かしてあげたいという思いを捨てずにご苦心してここまでこられたのですね。
dialogue.content: But you haven't just given up and looked away. You've struggled this far without letting go of the desire to do something for them.

dialogue.origin: そうですね。
dialogue.content: I suppose so.

dialogue.origin: まずあなたが他者のことで心を痛めることの中で、今は必要が無いものを少しずつ減らして正しいエネルギーに変えていけたら良いな、と思うのですがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.content: First, among the ways you feel pain for others, I wonder if we could gradually reduce what's not necessary right now and channel it into more constructive energy. How does that sound?

dialogue.origin: 必要がないものというのは具体的にどう見つければ良いでしょうか？
dialogue.content: What isn't necessary... how can I find that, specifically?

dialogue.origin: 今から色々とお話しする中で見つけられたらと思うのですが、いかがでしょうか。
dialogue.content: I was hoping we could discover that together as we talk more. How does that sound?

dialogue.origin: わかりました。よろしくお願いします
dialogue.content: Okay. Yes, please.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。いくつか質問させてくださいね。
dialogue.content: Thank you. Let me ask you a few questions.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: 理解をしてくれないというご家族は、あなたから見てどのような人柄・性格でしょうか？
dialogue.content: From your perspective, what kind of personalities do the family members who don't understand have?

dialogue.origin: 自分の意見を曲げることなく、自分に都合の悪いことはそもそも聞く耳を持たないし自分の価値観と異なるものはとことん悪としてみなすような感じです。
dialogue.content: They're the type who never change their minds, refuse to listen to anything inconvenient for them, and treat anything that differs from their own values as completely wrong.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。それは妹さんもでしょうか？
dialogue.content: I see. Is your sister like that too?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。みんなそんな感じです。
dialogue.content: Yes. They're all like that.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。妹さんはおいくつですか？
dialogue.content: I see. How old is your sister?

dialogue.origin: 18です
dialogue.content: She's 18.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。その年ごろですとまだ親の影響が強くありそうですがいかがですか？
dialogue.content: Thank you. At that age, it seems likely she'd still be strongly influenced by your parents. Would you agree?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。それにかなり父にべったりで父も妹にかなり甘く怒ることはありません。
dialogue.content: Yes. She's very attached to my father, and he spoils her a lot and never gets angry at her.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。それでは先ほどの人柄のお話はお父様やおばあさまの事をさしている部分が大きいでしょうか？
dialogue.content: I see. So when you described their personalities earlier, were you mostly referring to your father and grandmother?

dialogue.origin: そうですね、特に父です
dialogue.content: Yes, especially my father.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか。それでは、先ほどの上司の方はあなたから見てどのような人柄でしょうか？
dialogue.content: I understand. Then, how would you describe the personality of your boss?

dialogue.origin: フランクな感じで私に対してはいい人なのですが、仕事に関しては古い価値観で時間外労働なども当たり前であるとしちゃうような感じです。
dialogue.content: He's friendly and nice to me, but when it comes to work, he has old-fashioned values and thinks things like overtime are completely normal.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。確かに古い体質のようですね。それでは今の新人が戸惑うのも、あなたが間には入ってあげたくなるもの無理ないですね。
dialogue.content: I see. It certainly sounds like an old-fashioned mentality. It's no wonder the new hire is confused, and that you feel the urge to step in.

dialogue.origin: そうですね、今の価値観とはかなり離れているため戸惑うと思います
dialogue.content: Yes, I think she's confused because it's so out of step with current values.

dialogue.origin: いつの世もありますが、価値観が時代とともに変わってもついていける人間ばかりではないものですね。
dialogue.content: It's true of any era, but not everyone can keep up as values change with the times.

dialogue.origin: そうですね
dialogue.content: That's true.

dialogue.origin: 仮にあなたが思うようにお父様や上司の方に話ができたとして、すぐに言動を変えてくれる人達だと思いますか？
dialogue.content: Let's say you were able to speak to your father and your boss as you'd like. Do you think they are the kind of people who would change their words and actions right away?

dialogue.origin: 理解してもらえれば変えてもらえるんじゃないかっていう希望は持ってしまっていますね。
dialogue.content: I can't help but hope that if they understood, they might change.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね。それではあなたが彼らに声をかけようと思ったとき、どのような思いが浮かびますか？
dialogue.content: That makes sense. So, when you think about speaking to them, what kind of thoughts come to mind?

dialogue.origin: 先ほど「怖い」というフレーズもありましたが…。
dialogue.content: You mentioned feeling afraid earlier...

dialogue.origin: 声をかけても反論されてしまうし、まず聞いてもらうことが難しそうだなと思います
dialogue.content: I feel like even if I say something, they'll just argue back, and it seems difficult to even get them to listen in the first place.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。しっかりと話をする関係性に今はまだ無い、ということでしょうか？
dialogue.content: I see. So would you say you don't yet have the kind of relationship where you can have a serious talk?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。そもそもしっかり真面目に話を聞く体制に持っていくのが難しいと思います
dialogue.content: That's right. I think it's hard to even get them into a mindset to listen seriously.

dialogue.origin: 茶化される、というか真面目に取り合ってもらえないということでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Do you mean they would make light of it, or that they just wouldn't take you seriously?

dialogue.origin: そうですね、それと最後まで聞いてくれないことが多いです
dialogue.content: Yes, that, and they often don't listen until the end.

dialogue.origin: 父とかだと、話切る前に「でもそれは甘えてるからだろ」と遮られて話を切り上げられたりします
dialogue.content: With my father, for example, before I can finish speaking, he'll cut me off and end the conversation by saying something like, 'But that's just because she's being spoiled.'

dialogue.origin: 確かにそういう状況だと改めて声をかけるのをためらってしまいますよね。
dialogue.content: I can see how that kind of situation would make you hesitant to bring it up again.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 環境を変えても難しそうでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Do you think it would still be difficult even if you changed the setting?

dialogue.origin: どう言うことでしょうか？
dialogue.content: What do you mean?

dialogue.origin: 例えば、声を荒げにくい外のお店で話す、とか
dialogue.content: For example, talking in a public place like a cafe where it's harder to raise your voice.

dialogue.origin: 改めて一緒に主治医に話を聞いてもらって主治医からお話しいただくとか。
dialogue.content: Or having the attending physician explain it to them after you all go together.

dialogue.origin: それならできるかもしれません。
dialogue.content: That might be possible.

dialogue.origin: 身内に真意をつかれるのは、わかっているから余計に素直に聞けないという部分もあるかと思います。
dialogue.content: Sometimes, when it's a family member pointing out the truth, it can be harder for people to listen with an open mind, precisely because they already have some awareness of it.

dialogue.origin: それにお母様を取り巻くその環境は病状にとってマイナスにしかならないと思いますので、プロに冷静に説明してもらうことがご病気にとっても良いのではと思いますがいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Also, that environment surrounding your mother can only be detrimental to her condition. I think having a professional explain things calmly would be good for her illness as well. What do you think?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。一旦母に提案してみようと思います
dialogue.content: You're right. I'll try suggesting it to my mother first.

dialogue.origin: あなたはしっかりとした行動力をお持ちですね。
dialogue.content: You have a real capacity for taking action.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: Thank you.

dialogue.origin: まずはその一歩を踏み出す中で、次のステップが現れたらまたお話に来ていただけますか？
dialogue.content: As you take that first step, if a next step appears, would you be willing to come and talk about it again?

dialogue.origin: そうしてみます
dialogue.content: I'll do that.

dialogue.origin: あなたの、他者を想う行動力が少しでも自分にとってもお相手にとっても健康的な形で発揮されるようになると良いですね。
dialogue.content: I hope your caring drive to act for others can be expressed in a way that is healthy for both you and them.

dialogue.origin: そうですね。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Yes. Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: 頑張ってみます
dialogue.content: I'll do my best.

dialogue.origin: 心から応援しています。本日はお時間になってしまいましたが、ここまでお話しされてみていかがですか？
dialogue.content: I'm rooting for you. We're out of time for today, but how do you feel after talking about all of this?

dialogue.origin: 自分がそもそもなんで苦しくなってるかが紐解かれてよく理解できるたと思います。
dialogue.content: I feel like we've unraveled why I was struggling in the first place, and I understand it much better now.

dialogue.origin: 前に進めそうです
dialogue.content: I feel like I can move forward now.

dialogue.origin: それは良かったです。また是非ご自身のタイミングでお越しくださいね。
dialogue.content: I'm glad to hear that. Please feel free to come back again whenever the time feels right for you.

dialogue.origin: はい、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Okay, thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: 季節の変わり目ですので風邪などひかないようご自愛くださいね。それでは本日はここで失礼します。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: As the seasons change, please take good care of yourself and try not to catch a cold. We'll end here for today. Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: ★クライアント役ありがとうございました。後ほど率直なご意見をいただければ幸いです
dialogue.content: Thank you for playing the role of the client. I would appreciate your candid feedback later.

dialogue.origin: それでは終了させていただきます。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: Alright, I'll end the session now. Thank you.

topic.sub: 母の精神的健康に対する理解不足と家族間の意見不一致
